quizName: DMV Practice Test #2 30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: When wearing a jacket for protection, it should:

options.text: Be loose and flap in the wind while riding.

questions.explanation: Your jacket should fit snugly but not restrict your movement. It should not flap in the wind while you ride.

questions.question: As your motorcycle goes faster, you will:

options.text: Need to shift up through the gears.
Need to shift down through the gears.
Need to put the motorcycle in neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: Need to shift up through the gears.
questions.explanation: Shift into higher gears as your motorcycle speeds up.

questions.question: The best way to handle a tailgater is to:

options.text: Allow them to get in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow them to get in front of you.
questions.explanation: Let them pass you. If you speed up, they will just tailgate you at the higher speed, which is more dangerous.

questions.question: What should be your first priority when buying a motorcycle helmet?
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that protects you best. Pick one that fastens securely, fits correctly, and is DOT-approved.

questions.question: Should you wear gloves while riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Yes. Your hands may get cold while riding.
Yes. They improve your grip and protect your hands.
No. Gloves interfere with the controls.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes. They improve your grip and protect your hands.
questions.explanation: Gloves improve your grip and protect your hands. Use full-fingered gloves made of durable material.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. This sign warns you that a stop sign is coming up.

questions.question: Having one alcoholic drink before riding:

options.text: Will not lead to a DUI conviction.
Will never affect your riding skills.
Can affect your ability to operate a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can affect your ability to operate a motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Even one drink can affect your riding ability. You can be convicted of riding impaired even if you are below the legal alcohol limit.

questions.question: If vehicles or hazards are to your right, ride on which side of your lane?
questions.explanation: Position yourself to have the most space. If hazards are on your right, ride on the left side of your lane.

questions.question: No matter which helmet style you choose, you get the most protection by making sure it:
questions.explanation: Get maximum protection by choosing a DOT-approved helmet that fits snugly all the way around with no damage.

questions.question: Which material provides the best protection for motorcycle riders?
questions.explanation: Leather and sturdy synthetic materials provide the best protection for motorcycle riders.

questions.question: Do motorcycle mirrors have blind spots?

options.text: No, because motorcycles are smaller than cars.

questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots, just like cars. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: What lane position should you choose?

options.text: A position that makes you visible and keeps safe space around you.
Any position you like, regardless of other vehicles.
A position close to other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: A position that makes you visible and keeps safe space around you.
questions.explanation: Position yourself where other drivers can see you and where you have space around your motorcycle. The best lane position changes based on road conditions. Good riders adjust their position as needed.

questions.question: What is the danger of long-term wind noise exposure?

options.text: It can cause permanent hearing damage.
It is just a normal part of riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can cause permanent hearing damage.
questions.explanation: Long-term wind noise can permanently damage your hearing. Wear ear protection while riding. Good ear protection lets you hear important sounds like sirens and car horns.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. They warn drivers about upcoming road conditions. This sign warns you that a railroad crossing is ahead.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow traffic light mean?

options.text: The light is about to turn red.
The light is about to turn green.
Stop and wait for traffic to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: The light is about to turn red.
questions.explanation: A yellow light warns you that the signal will change to red soon. Slow down and stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection, continue through.

questions.question: What should you do if you borrow a motorcycle?

options.text: Assume all controls are in the same place as on your motorcycle.
Take it out on the highway right away.
Practice with it in a controlled area first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Practice with it in a controlled area first.
questions.explanation: Every motorcycle is different. Before riding an unfamiliar motorcycle, learn where all the controls are. Practice in a safe area before riding on the road.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign is placed on the back of slow-moving vehicles that travel under 25 mph. Examples include farm equipment, construction vehicles, and horse-drawn vehicles.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. They warn drivers about upcoming road conditions. This sign warns that the right lane will end ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Vehicles will enter the roadway ahead.
Stop completely and go when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and go when safe.
questions.explanation: Red octagonal signs are always stop signs. When you see one, come to a complete stop. Yield to traffic and pedestrians, then proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: How should a motorcycle jacket fit?

options.text: Loosely so it flaps in the wind.
Snugly so it does not flap in the wind.
It should not be made of leather or sturdy material.

questions.correctAnswerText: Snugly so it does not flap in the wind.
questions.explanation: Wear pants and a jacket made of leather or sturdy material. They should fit snugly enough to not flap in the wind, but loose enough to let you move freely.

questions.question: What is the best way to prevent fatigue on a long trip?

options.text: Limit how much you ride each day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Limit how much you ride each day.
questions.explanation: On long trips, take frequent breaks to rest even if you are not tired. Most experienced riders do not ride more than six hours a day. Wind, cold, and rain make you tired faster, so dress to protect yourself from the weather.

questions.question: What can happen if you lock your brakes?
questions.explanation: Locking the brakes can cause you to lose control. If your front brake locks, release it and apply it again. If you lock your rear brake on dry pavement, keep it locked until you stop completely.

questions.question: What item will you NOT be asked to identify during the motorcycle skills test pre-trip inspection?
questions.explanation: Before your skills test, you will be asked to identify the starter, kill switch, clutch (if your motorcycle has one), throttle, gear selector, headlight dimmer switch, brakes, turn signals, and horn.

questions.question: What can happen if a motorcycle rider takes a turn too fast?

options.text: They have more control of the motorcycle.
They may accidentally leave the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may accidentally leave the road.
questions.explanation: Taking a turn too fast can cause you to lose control of your motorcycle. It may cross into another lane or go off the road.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT recommended protective clothing for motorcycle riders?
questions.explanation: Wear protective clothing when riding a motorcycle. Good protective items include long-sleeved jackets, long heavy pants, boots that cover your ankles, and full-fingered leather gloves. Cover as much skin as possible.

questions.question: When stopping, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Get into the habit of using both the front and rear brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: What should you do when riding at night?

options.text: Ride on the left side of the lane to see around vehicles ahead.
Ride close to the vehicle in front of you to use their headlights.
Reduce your speed so you can avoid unexpected hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed so you can avoid unexpected hazards.
questions.explanation: Always ride at a lower speed at night than you would during the day. This gives you a better chance of avoiding hazards. Also increase your distance from other vehicles and be flexible with your lane position.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?

options.text: During the day and at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: During the day and at night.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen in daylight, so wear bright, reflective clothing while riding at any time of day.

questions.question: What is the best footwear for motorcycle riders?
questions.explanation: Leather boots offer the best protection for riders. They should be high and sturdy enough to cover and support your ankles.

questions.question: What must a motorcycle helmet meet by law?

options.text: Be free of stickers or artwork.
Be a dark color to avoid glare.

questions.explanation: All riders and passengers must wear a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation safety standards. The helmet manufacturer must certify that it meets federal standards.
